newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's interim cabinet plans to free prices.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's interim cabinet plans to free prices.

text.p: Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet will liberalise some prices to speed up market reforms and overcome shortages of basic commodities, Trade Minister Daniela Bobeva said on Monday.
"Bulgaria's interim cabinet is starting liberalising prices of basic goods as the only way to overcome shortages," Bobeva told reporters after a cabinet meeting.
International lenders have urged the government to lift all price controls on basic goods and utilities like power, heating and other services.
Controls on bread and grain prices lead to shortages, and to counter-act them the cabinet unlocked 50,000 tonnes of grain from state reserves and partly freed prices of grain and bread.

"So far Bulgaria could not afford to lift completely state control over grain and bread prices. We will try to keep the price affordable for the population despite difficulties we may face with international lenders," said Agriculture Minister Roumen Christov.
He said the price of bread would rise from its present 300 levs per kilogramme.
"The price at which grain will be sold is set at $85 per tonne or around 50 percent of the market price, so the bread price will be around 600 levs per kilogramme," Christov said.
Releasing the state reserve will give Bulgaria a total of about 80,000 tonnes of grain, enough to meet bread demand for the next month, Christov said.
"All we could decide so far towards liberalisation of prices is that we lift restrictions on prices offered by local grain producers. They are allowed to sell grain at $100 per tonne," he said.
The agriculture ministry estimates private local producers could provide 20,000 to 30,000 tonnes of grain at that price.
The caretaker cabinet decided on Monday, ahead of this week's negotiations with international lenders, to increase minimum monthly wages and social benefits by 60 percent from March 1.
The former Socialist cabinet doubled the minimum wage last month to keep pace with soaring inflation.
"The minimum monthly wage will be set at 17,600 levs and pensioners will receive 10,000 levs in addition," Social Care Minister Ivan Neikov told reporters.
"An effective safety net for the poorest must be devised before any further abolition of price controls," Neikov said.
The trade ministry submitted a proposal to replace fixed prices for cigarettes and tobacco with a minimum price.
New cigarette prices, expected to be at least double the current price, will be announced later on Monday, Bobeva said.
She said that Thursday's cabinet meeting would discuss increasing medicine prices and lifting price controls on them.
A recent hike on fuel prices, which were also subsidised so far, helped the government overcome a crippling fuel shortage. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 8569
